content.value_statement: Angular performance issues can hide in change detection, data fetching, bundles, rendering, and hydration. This skill applies prioritized modern Angular patterns during implementation, review, and refactoring.
actual_capabilities: Reviews components for OnPush change detection, signals, standalone architecture, and zoneless compatibility.
Identifies sequential data fetching and recommends RxJS parallelization or dependency-aware flattening.
Recommends lazy routes, dynamic imports, and deferred components to reduce initial bundles.
Evaluates list rendering, template expressions, pure pipes, computed signals, and virtual scrolling.
Guides SSR data transfer, incremental hydration, event replay, and deferred hydration.
Finds manual subscription patterns and recommends lifecycle-aware cleanup or signal conversion.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not execute audits, builds, or benchmarks automatically.
Examples favor modern Angular APIs and may require adaptation for older versions.
Recommendations require project-specific testing and production performance validation.
Cannot assess dependencies, runtime data, or deployment settings unless they are provided.

use_cases.title: Build Efficient Angular Features
use_cases.description: Apply modern component, state, routing, and rendering patterns while implementing new features.

use_cases.title: Review Performance Regressions
use_cases.description: Prioritize likely bottlenecks in change detection, data fetching, templates, bundles, and subscriptions.

use_cases.title: Improve SSR Delivery
use_cases.description: Plan server data loading, TransferState, hydration, and deferred content for faster page delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.prompt:
Review this Angular component for performance issues. Check change detection, signals, template work, list tracking, and subscription cleanup. Explain each recommendation simply.

Component: [paste component]
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single component

prompt_templates.title: Remove Request Waterfalls
prompt_templates.prompt:
Refactor the provided Angular feature to remove sequential requests. Use forkJoin for independent calls and switchMap for dependent calls. Preserve behavior and explain tradeoffs.

Feature: [paste code]

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Bundle and Rendering Cost
prompt_templates.prompt:
Audit this Angular route and component set for bundle size and rendering performance. Recommend lazy routes, dynamic imports, @defer triggers, and virtual scrolling where appropriate.

Files: [paste relevant files]

prompt_templates.title: Audit SSR and Hydration
prompt_templates.prompt:
Review this Angular SSR implementation. Evaluate hydration, TransferState, server data loading, browser-only APIs, and deferred content. Produce prioritized findings and validation steps.

Implementation: [paste files]

output_examples.input: Review a product list that uses default change detection, tracks by index, and renders 5,000 rows.
output_examples.output: Priority: High. Use OnPush and signal-backed state. Track stable product IDs. Add CDK virtual scrolling, then measure rendering and interaction latency.

output_examples.input: Assess an SSR page that repeats API requests after hydration.
output_examples.output: Priority: High. Cache server-fetched data with TransferState, read it in the browser, and remove consumed entries. Verify one request per navigation.

output_examples.input: Reduce the initial bundle for an analytics route with a chart library.
output_examples.output: Priority: Critical. Lazy-load the route and chart library. Defer non-critical charts by viewport or interaction. Confirm chunk sizes with the project build analyzer.

best_practices: Provide the Angular version, relevant files, architecture, and current performance evidence.
Prioritize recommendations by measured user impact, implementation risk, and framework compatibility.
Run tests, builds, accessibility checks, and performance measurements after each meaningful refactor.
anti_patterns: Applying every recommendation without checking Angular version or project constraints.
Using index-based list tracking when items have stable identifiers.
Claiming performance gains without before-and-after measurements.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my project automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review and refactoring guidance. Your agent may edit files only when your request and tool permissions allow it.

faq.question: Which Angular versions does it target?
faq.answer: Examples favor modern Angular APIs, including signals, standalone components, new control flow, zoneless change detection, and incremental hydration.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy Angular applications?
faq.answer: Yes, but some recommendations require adaptation. Provide your Angular version, architecture, and compatibility constraints for relevant advice.

faq.question: Does it measure performance?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend metrics and validation steps, but it does not run benchmarks unless the agent receives tools and project access.

faq.question: Does it cover server-side rendering?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers server data loading, TransferState, hydration, event replay, deferred hydration, and browser-server boundaries.

faq.question: Can it replace expert performance review?
faq.answer: No. Validate recommendations against application behavior, accessibility, security, browser support, and production performance data.
